What makes Quetzalcoatlus so amazing?

With wings spread as wide as a small airplane, Quetzalcoatlus is a candidate for the largest flying animal in history. It stood as tall as a giraffe, too.

content.text:
Nature and science facts about Quetzalcoatlus

Quetzalcoatlus had a wingspan of about 10–11m (up to 12m), and when it raised its head it stood 4–5m tall—as tall as a giraffe. It had no teeth. Today the leading idea is the "terrestrial predator" hypothesis—that it walked the ground like a stork, hunting small dinosaurs and lizards. According to a 2021 study, it probably leapt about 2.5m off the ground and then took off with powerful wingbeats. Its fossils are found in Texas, USA.

Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Stretch a 10m tape measure across the floor so your child can really feel the wingspan. Compare it with photos of giraffes and storks, and imagine together "How could an animal this big fly?" to build interest.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. How big was Quetzalcoatlus?
A. It had a wingspan of about 10–11m and stood 4–5m tall—as tall as a giraffe. It's a candidate for the largest flying animal in history.

Q. Did it move around on the ground too?
A. Yes. The leading "terrestrial predator" hypothesis suggests it walked the ground like a stork, hunting small dinosaurs and lizards.

Q. How can we enjoy it at home?
A. Try stretching out a 10m tape measure and comparing it with giraffes and storks.
